title: Introduce invocation-phase translation layer and noise-gate alert pruner
author: Noah Rivera
description:
Context and motivation: production SREs have been chasing noisy, long-tail token/phase alerts and translating per-stage runtime metrics between components (gateway, router, runtime, kv-shard) requires brittle ad-hoc mappings. This PR introduces a lightweight translation layer that normalizes per-invocation phase metrics into a single schema and an alert-pruner that applies a noise-gating policy using enrichment signals (span fidelity, sampled-kv-hits, model-variant fallback reasons) before firing high-cost SLO alerts.

What this PR does (high level): adds telemetry.translate service (go) that consumes raw phase-level counters and emits unified metrics (invocation.phase.latency_ms, invocation.phase.cpu_ms, invocation.phase.token_cost) with consistent tags; implements an alert_pruner daemon (python) that subscribes to candidate alerts and applies a rules engine to suppress or downgrade noisy alerts when enrichment indicates long-tail noise or correlated kernel warmups; introduces a new dashboard (Grafana JSON) for phase-aligned sparkline rollups and an alertplaybook doc for on-call runbooks.

Design notes: translation layer is intentionally append-only and idempotent: it keeps a small mapping table for phases discovered at runtime and emits a canonical phase key (input, encode, kv-lookup, decode, stream-emit). The alert-pruner uses a configurable scoring heuristic (prefers high fidelity spans, significant token_cost delta, repeated occurrence within tenant sessions) and supports adaptive suppression windows (per-tenant, per-route). Both components include feature flags for gradual rollout and telemetry-only mode for 48h observation.

Checklist: - [x] translation service protobufs and v1 schema - [x] alert-pruner rules engine + unit tests - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + panels (phase-sparklines, pruner-action-log) - [x] e2e smoke test in perf-canary harness - [x] docs: alertplaybook.md, rollout notes - [x] feature flags gated behind rollout/telemetry-experiment

Commits summary: commit 1/6: add telemetry.translate service skeleton and proto definitions; commit 2/6: implement canonical phase mapper and emit adapters for StatsD/OTel; commit 3/6: initial alert_pruner daemon and rule DSL with unit tests; commit 4/6: Grafana dashboard and dashboard migration script; commit 5/6: add perf-canary integration test and sample workloads; commit 6/6: docs, release notes and feature-flag config.

Files changed (high level): sources/redwood/telemetry/translate/main.go; sources/redwood/telemetry/translate/proto/phase.proto; sources/redwood/alerting/pruner/pruner.py; sources/redwood/alerting/pruner/rules/*.py; sources/redwood/grafana/dashboards/phase-translation-pruner.json; docs/oncall/alertplaybook-telemetry-pruner.md; infra/flags/rollout/telemetry_translate.yaml; tests/perf_canary/translate_pruner_smoke.py; Makefile and CI config tweaks. Small illustrative snippet added to phase.proto to show canonical enum of phases but no large diffs included.

Review conversation (summary):
- Ava Patel (review): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: 1) make the prune decision deterministic when scores tie, and 2) make the suppression window bounded per-tenant. Also request a short stress test for the scoring path."
- Noah Rivera (author): "Addressed both: tie-breaker uses last-successful-fallback timestamp and windows are capped by a tenant-configurable max; added stress test under tests/sanity/pruner_stress.py."
- Liam Chen (review): "Can we add a label to pruner actions that we can backfill into traces so alerts can be unpruned for retrospective investigations?"
- Noah Rivera: "Added pruner_action tag emitted as an OTel attribute and a small handler that writes a compact pruner log into the observability bucket for 7 days."
- Sofia Martinez (approval): "Verified e2e smoke in perf-canary and validated that disabled mode produces no suppression. Approving for squash-merge."

CI details: initial CI run had a flaky test in alerting/rules/test_similarity.py; rerun fixed by adding a 10ms sleep in the test harness (comment included on the test); all checks subsequently passed (unit, integration, lint, go vet).

Merge outcome: merged via squash by Noah Rivera. Release notes included; feature flagged and rolled out to 10% of tenants for 72h observation, then 100% if no regression.

Operational considerations: - telemetry.translate uses bounded memory for phase mapping (eviction LRU after 10k distinct phase keys) to prevent high-cardinality blowups. - pruner emits metrics for suppressed_alerts.count and pruner_score.hist which are forwarded to the SLO dashboard. - added an internal alert to detect if pruner suppression exceeds 20% of candidate alerts for more than 15 minutes to avoid silent mass suppression.

Rollout plan: 1) telemetry-only mode (48h) on staging; 2) 10% traffic in prod with suppression disabled (emit only) 24h; 3) enable soft suppression at 10% tenants for 72h; 4) increase to 100% with a 24h monitoring window and automatic rollback if error-rate or SLO regressions exceed thresholds.

Related work / references: ENG-4523 (observability long-tail workstream), ENG-4599 (alerts playbook refactor), SUP-9871 (customer-facing noise tickets).

release_notes: Introduce invocation-phase translation and a configurable alert-pruner to reduce noisy long-tail SLO alerts. Features are feature-flagged and rolled out progressively. Adds new metrics (pruner.suppressed_alerts, pruner.score_hist) and a Grafana dashboard.
notes_for_oncall: If increased suppression is observed, check pruner.score_hist and pruner.suppressed_alerts and run `pruner/inspect.py --tenant=<tenant>` to dump recent actions. The pruner has a safety alert if suppression >20% for 15m.
